newsitem.title: INDIA: Reserve Bank of India buys dollars at lower level.
newsitem.headline: Reserve Bank of India buys dollars at lower level.

text.p: The rupee closed at 35.840/850 against the dollar on Friday, firming from an open at 35.85/86 in quiet trading, dealers said.
The day was marked by poor demand for dollars and normal supplies, causing the rupee to appreciate, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the only serious buyer of the dollar on Friday, bought dollars at 35.8450 level compared to its earlier purchase price of 35.85, they said.
Forward dollar premia continued to be easy, reflecting the easy liqudity in the money market, dealers said.
The 6-month annualised premium ended at 7.37 percent on Friday compared to the previous 7.25 percent, dealers said.
"The market does not believe easy conditions will last long," said a bank dealer. "With successive repos absorbing higher amounts, there exists a risk of flare up in call and premia."
